Championing Childhood
Championing Childhood
Championing Childhood
Championing Childhood
Nestled within 60 acres of stunning Oxfordshire countryside, just five miles from Oxford, we are a leading independent day school for boys and girls aged 2–11.
Our enviable location is matched by our commitment to exceptional academic achievement, heartfelt pastoral care, and outstanding facilities. These include bright, modern classrooms and state-of-the-art spaces dedicated to Science, Art, Music, Design, and Food Technology. Our extensive sports facilities and private rural grounds, complete with a low-ropes course set in a magical bluebell wood, further enhance the learning experience.
At our school, your child will discover endless opportunities to unlock their true potential.

pageCache.pageTitle: Partnerships - Chandlings Independent Prep School - Oxford
pageCache.text:
Partnerships
At Chandlings Prep, we believe in the power of community and collaboration.
Our partnership initiatives extend our resources and expertise beyond our school gates, fostering connections with local schools and enriching the educational landscape of our area. These partnerships not only benefit the wider community but also provide valuable experiences for our own students, teaching them the importance of sharing and community engagement.
Outdoor Learning: Sharing Nature’s Classroom
We’re proud to open our expansive grounds to a local primary school for weekly outdoor learning sessions. Led by our experienced staff, these sessions allow children from our partner school to benefit from our fantastic outdoor facilities, fostering a love for nature and experiential learning.
Swimming: Making a Splash
Our swimming pool is a valuable resource that we’re delighted to share. Each week, students from a local primary school visit Chandlings to receive swimming lessons from our qualified staff. This initiative helps ensure that more children in our community have the opportunity to learn this crucial life skill.
Sports Tournaments: Fostering Friendly Competition
We regularly host sports tournaments involving several local primary schools. These events provide an excellent opportunity for children to engage in friendly competition, develop sportsmanship, and make new friends. We’re pleased to offer access to our pitches and courts to support these community sporting events.
Author Visits: Inspiring Young Readers
When we host visiting authors, we extend invitations to local schools. These events inspire a love of reading and writing across our wider community, allowing more children to benefit from these enriching experiences.
Work Experience: Nurturing Future Educators
We are developing relationships with local schools to provide work experience placements. This initiative allows older students to gain valuable insights into the world of education, potentially inspiring the next generation of teachers.
Local Community
At Chandlings Prep, we’re committed to being an active, positive force in our local community. Through these partnerships, we aim to share our resources, expertise, and passion for education as widely as possible. We believe that by working together, we can create a richer, more diverse educational experience for all children in our area.
New Partnerships
We’re always open to new partnership opportunities that align with our values and can benefit the wider community. If you represent a local school or organisation and are interested in partnering with Chandlings Prep, we’d love to hear from you.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wellbeing & Pastoral Care - Chandlings Independent Prep School - Oxford
pageCache.text:
Wellbeing & Pastoral Care
Our approach to pastoral care is holistic, proactive, and deeply woven into the fabric of school life.
We strive to create an environment where every child feels valued, supported, and empowered to thrive both academically and personally.
Chandlings Values: Our school values are the guiding principles that shape our community.
These are prominently displayed and regularly discussed, ensuring they remain at the forefront of our daily interactions.
Each half-term, we focus on a specific topic related to our values, which is creatively presented on our ever-changing blackboard.
We celebrate kindness through our termly Kindness Cup, recognising those who go above and beyond in showing compassion to others. Our house point system, Deputy Head awards, and Excellence awards further reinforce positive behaviours and achievements, encouraging children to embody our values in all aspects of their school life.
The Wellbeing Knight
Central to our wellbeing approach is ‘The Wellbeing Knight’, a symbol developed collaboratively with our school community and through pupil voice. This character embodies our commitment to nurturing each child’s emotional and mental health alongside their academic growth.
We’re proud to have been re-awarded the UK’s highest wellbeing accolade – the National Children’s Bureau-backed Wellbeing Award for Schools (WAS). This recognition affirms our dedication to placing wellbeing at the heart of our educational ethos. We firmly believe that a child’s wellbeing and academic development are intrinsically linked, and our approach reflects this understanding.
House System
Our house system, comprising Richardson, Astley, and Poltimore houses, fosters a sense of belonging and friendly competition. Through house activities, children learn teamwork, develop leadership skills, and form friendships across year groups, contributing to a strong and supportive school community.
Safeguarding
The safety and welfare of our pupils and staff are paramount. We are committed to providing a happy, caring, and safe environment where children can learn free from any form of abuse. Safeguarding is everyone’s responsibility at Chandlings, and all staff receive regular training to ensure they can identify signs of distress and confidently apply safeguarding processes.
PSHEE (Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education)
Our weekly PSHEE lessons are a cornerstone of our wellbeing curriculum. These sessions provide a safe space for open discussions on a wide range of topics, from personal safety and positive friendships to celebrating differences. The programme is flexible, allowing us to address the immediate needs of each class as they arise.
PSHEE themes are reinforced through assemblies, creating a cohesive approach to personal development. We also invite visitors to enhance the curriculum, providing diverse perspectives and real-world insights.
RHSE (Relationships, Health and Sex Education)
Our high-quality RHSE programme equips pupils with the knowledge, understanding, skills, and confidence to navigate the complexities of society. The age-specific curriculum ensures that information is presented appropriately, helping children develop healthy relationships and make informed decisions about their health and wellbeing.
Every Child’s Voice Matters
Our thriving School Council gives children the opportunity to contribute to school improvements and develop skills. We value pupil input through pastoral surveys and various ambassador roles, including Eco Ambassadors, School Council Ambassadors, and representatives for Sports, Technology, Language, Library, and Wellbeing.
We even involve our pupils in choosing the charities we support, fostering a sense of social responsibility and empathy from a young age.
Multi-Layered Support
Our pastoral care system is multi-layered, ensuring comprehensive support for every child. At the heart of this system is the Form Teacher, who plays a crucial role in overseeing each child’s overall welfare and happiness. However, all staff contribute to the care and support of our pupils, creating a network of trusted adults who children can turn to when needed.
We use an information tracking system that allows staff to share insights, creating a seamless support structure around each child. This approach of listening and noticing ensures we understand and can support each child individually.
Transparency and collaboration with parents are paramount in our pastoral approach. We value strong links with families and work together to ensure the most positive experience for each child.
Our age-specific behaviour policies underscore the importance of reflection and making appropriate choices, helping children develop self-awareness and emotional intelligence.
Find Out More

pageCache.pageTitle: Senior School Destinations - Chandlings Independent Prep School - Oxford
pageCache.text:
Independent Senior School Destinations
Our children consistently secure places at established and highly regarded secondary schools. These renowned institutions have a strong track record of academic excellence and provide exceptional opportunities for our children’s continued education and personal development. Year over year, students enjoy early acceptances, awards and scholarships.
We are pleased to host a large Secondary Schools Fair on a biannual basis, where pupils and their parents can speak directly to 30+ regional senior school representatives. Not only does this highlight our fortified partnerships with these schools, but it provides families with a convenient way to explore initial options for their child.
A post shared by Chandlings Prep School (@chandlings_school)

pageCache.pageTitle: Clubs & Activities - Chandlings Independent Prep School - Oxford
pageCache.text:
Clubs & Activities
Activity Category
Term
Year Group
Strand
Journalism
Children have the opportunity to contribute to the new Chandlings pupils’ newspaper. We are looking for writers, photographers, interviewers, editors and illustrators.
Library Lunchtime Club
Discover exciting books and authors whilst sharing your own favourites with friends. Listen to stories and join in a variety of book-related craft activities.
History Detectives
Children have the opportunity to explore a variety of primary and secondary sources to build up a picture of a historical period or a key figure from the past.
Debating Club
Debating club allows children to build confidence, public speaking, and critical thinking skills while exploring and debating exciting topics.
Young Filmmakers
Young Filmmakers will learn and use different practical techniques used in films, storyboarding, scriptwriting, and editing to create a film of their own.
Tech Ambassadors
Join the Year 6 Tech Ambassadors who will run a technology based club. Dive into coding, robotics, and digital skills.
SSNAP Knitting Club
SSNAP are running low on their supply of baby blankets for the neonatal unit at the JR hospital. Together we would like to create some.
Gardening Club
Join Mr Foster in the school grounds for Gardening Club to learn gardening techniques and vegetable growing skills whilst harvesting vegetables once ready.
Outdoor Adventure
Join Mr Umhoefer and Mr Judd to explore the grounds and take part in team challenges such as orienteering and hide and seek for Outdoor Adventure club.
Let’s Doodle
This is a fun and calming session during which the children can enjoy the simple art of drawing and get lost in the creative world of doodling.
Mindfulness
Mindfulness includes calming activities such as children’s yoga, word searches, dot to dot, spot the difference, sudoku, and mindfulness colouring.
Yoga & Wellbeing
Yoga helps children maintain their innate flexibility, develop muscular strength and endurance, and improve coordination. Elements of mindfulness and wellbeing are also part of the sessions.
Juggling & Circus Skills
Children learn to juggle, spin plates, use a diablo, and more! They have fun practising all the skills needed to put together their own mini performances.
Bright Sparks Science
These sessions teach your child about active science exploration, logic and problem solving, teamwork, and good communication skills. A different topic/theme is explored each term.
STEM Club
Allows children to tackle exciting challenges in science, technology, engineering, and math, developing critical thinking and teamwork.
Lego Creator Club
This club formed from suggestions by the school council. Children join Mrs Biggs every week in their pursuit to build their very own Lego Creator model.
Textile Design Club
Children design their own pattern digitally before printing on fabric using sublimation printing. The fabric is then used to make a product that is unique such as a pencil case or wash bag.
Little Builders
Little Builders club is designed for young engineers of the future to design, draw and build a variety of structures.
Furniture Making
Furniture Makers club allows children to design a piece of furniture and go through the planning stages of how to make it before building it themselves whilst learning DIY skills.
3D Printing
As part of 3D Printing club, the children learn how to use the TinkerCad software to design and make small objects using the 3D Printers.
Construction Club
Children will design, build, and problem-solve with fun, hands-on activities using different materials such as LEGO, wood, and more.
Art Scholars
Refine artistic skills, experiment with advanced techniques, and build an inspiring portfolio. Suitable for those wanting to take their art skills to the next level.
Art Club
Art Club is available for all abilities and is an opportunity for children to develop core techniques in Art including painting, drawing, and sculpting.
Arts & Craft
This involves creating hands-on projects exploring painting, drawing, and crafting techniques. It’s a fun but structured club combining art skills with craft.
Creative Craft
Our Creative Craft club provides children the chance to explore their creative side by exploring a variety of different crafts activities.
Summer Fun
Come and enjoy a range of Summer Fun activities during the Summer Term. We will be reading summer themed stories, making summer crafts, and venturing outside into the sunshine.
Once upon a storytime
The children unwind at the end of the day whilst losing themselves in classic stories and exploring the themes and characters that they know and love.
Imagination Stations
The children are able to practice their story telling skills through play-based learning. They are given the opportunity to imagine different characters in different settings and role-play their own narratives.
Ukuleles
Suitable for all abilities including those with no previous experience. Children will strum fun tunes, learn chords, and perform in a supportive group perfect for beginners.
Guitar & Ukuleles Group
Suitable for all abilities including those with no previous experience. Children will learn chords, rhythm, and fun group songs.
Windband
This ensemble is for wind players in the older years who learn the flute, oboe, clarinet, bassoon, trumpet, french horn, saxophone, trombone, or other wind instruments.
Orchestra
Any child who has been learning (violin, cello, double bass, trumpet, trombone, french horn, flute, clarinet, oboe, bassoon, drums) for 2+ terms is recommended to join.
Percussion Club
This termly ensemble is for children who wish to learn how to play the drums, xylophones, and an array of other percussion instruments depending on their interests.
Keyboard Club
Explore piano basics, chords, and melodies in an engaging group environment. This is for all abilities including those who wish to start learning.
Recorder Club
Learn to read music and perform melodies, progressing from simple tunes to harmonised pieces. This is for all abilities including those who wish to start learning.
String Orchestra
This is suitable for those who have been practicing the violin, viola, cello, or double bass for 2+ terms. It’s an opportunity to play beautiful ensemble pieces in a group.
Prep Lower Strings
Children who are in Year 3-6 and have cell or double bass lessons are able to Prep Lower Strings, learning how to play with others and develop their performance skills.
Pre Prep Singers
This club allows children to develop a love for music through fun songs, vocal exercises, and group performances in an encouraging setting.
Chamber Choir
Auditions for this group happen in the preceding summer term and this ensemble is then locked for the year. New school starters may apply for an audition.
Music & Movement
A time to be creative with musical instruments and move our bodies to the beat, it’s a fun activity for all children combining music and movement.
Musical Theatre
Musical Theatre club is a wonderful way for the children to learn new skills and build confidence, inspiring plenty of creativity along the way they learn a variety of songs, dances, and creative play.
Choral Speaking
Improve vocal clarity, expression, and rhythm through engaging group poetry and dramatic recitations. Children don’t need to be studying LAMDA to participate.
Creation Drama
As well as developing their performance skills, Creation will also inspire the children to read in full the stories they are rehearsing and also research the issues, settings and historical context of the works.
Ballet
This is a fun yet disciplined class offering children the chance to learn from the highly prestigious Royal Academy of Dance ballet syllabus with the option to participate in exams.
Modern Dance
Dance, exercise and have fun learning dance steps and simple routines. Children will learn how to choreograph short pieces to a variety of music whilst learning about timing, rhythm and performance work.
Karate
Sensai Patience Kakitie who runs this activity is a board member of the English Karate Federation. This session is now longer in duration and open to all abilities and those new to Karate.
Gymnastics Squad
This club is designed to extend those pupils who have shown an aptitude for gymnastics during the Gymnastics clubs in the Autumn and Spring term and who would like to expand their skills further.
Gymnastics
Children will be taught the basics of gymnastics through floor work and simple apparatus. By the end of the term they will perform a choreographed routine including elements learned during the club.
Trampolining
We have our own trampolines in which children can build aerial skills, strength, and confidence by mastering flips, routines, and precise techniques.
CycleTots
CycleTots are super fun balance bike classes that help little ones develop the core skills of balancing, grow in confidence, and build on the skills used by those already pedalling.
Archery
Sessions are run by qualified specialists and children will develop their aim and precision with a bow and arrow, working towards shooting accurately.
Golf
Sessions are run by professionals from Frilford Heath Golf Club and all abilities are welcome. The younger year children use specially modified clubs and balls in order to learn about the game.
Football
Mr Todd provides the children with a fun introduction to football. This activity will help your child improve coordination and team skills whilst learning basic football skills.
Football
Our external coaches aim to develop, nurture and motivate all players who attend. They also have very close links with a number of professional clubs & scouts including Oxford United F.C.
Tennis
An external Tennis coach comes into the school and leads the sessions. It’s open to children of all ability levels and is tailored for them as they progress in their Tennis skills.
Sports Scholars
This is more suitable for children who want to focus on advanced techniques, fitness, and sportsmanship to excel in sports.
Cricket
Children will learn the perfect batting, bowling, and fielding skills while learning the strategy and spirit of this classic sport.
Prep Football
Learn how to enhance ball control including accuracy when passing and scoring, as well as learning how to work as a team.
Netball
Netball club allows children to practice passing, shooting, and positional play, developing teamwork and court awareness in competitive matches.
Basketball
All abilities are welcome as children will learn dribbling, shooting, and game strategies while building agility, coordination, and team spirit.
Boys Hockey
Boys’ Hockey will help children to improve passing and defending skills, whilst getting the opportunity to compete against other teams.
Girls Hockey
Girls Hockey helps to build teamwork, stick skills, and strategic play while competing in dynamic and fast-paced games against other teams.
Athletics Club
Suitable for those who want to improve their running, jumping, and throwing techniques to enhance speed, strength, and overall athletic ability.
Cross Country Club
Children will learn to develop endurance, pacing, and resilience while improving cross country running skills and general fitness.
Technical Swimming
The sessions are aimed at those Prep swimmers who can swim over 50m and are now looking to build both speed and endurance in preparation for school squad or club swimming.
Swimming
The sessions are aimed at children who find it difficult to swim 25m using a recognised swimming stroke. They aim to promote water confidence and develop basic stroke techniques.
Swim Squad
Swim Squad is designed as an extensions for the most able swimmers in the school developing advanced stroke technique whilst building stamina and speed alongside learning race tactics.
Pony Rangers
Children will benefit from activities where riding isn’t essential. They will develop their interaction with animals, understand their behaviour, and improve their confidence around the ponies.
Riding
With our very own horses and stables on-site, children immerse themselves in all aspects of equestrian care and each lesson builds toward Association of British Riding Schools Rosette Awards.

pageCache.pageTitle: Extra-Curricular Programme - Chandlings Independent Prep School - Oxford
pageCache.text:
Extra-Curricular Programme
Our Extra-Curricular Programme is designed to:
Ignite passions, develop skills, and create unforgettable childhood memories against the stunning backdrop of 60 acres of Oxfordshire countryside.
Sports
Children can dive into swimming, perfect their swing on the golf course, or develop equestrian skills in our riding arena.
Creative Arts
Budding artists, musicians, and performers find plenty of opportunities to express themselves and hone their craft.
Academic Enrichment
For those with a thirst for knowledge, we offer clubs that delve deeper into subjects like science, technology, and languages.
Outdoor Adventures
Our expansive grounds provide the perfect setting for nature exploration, gardening, and outdoor skills development.
Exceptional Facilities
— Our exceptional facilities provide the perfect canvas for children to create their own adventures. From our full-size Astroturf and swimming pool, to the horse riding arena and 9-hole golf course, every corner of our campus invites exploration and discovery.
Flexibility and Accessibility
We understand that every child is unique, with their own interests and schedules. That’s why we’ve designed our programme to be as flexible and accessible as possible:
Activities are thoughtfully scheduled before, during, and after school to accommodate different family routines.
Many activities are teacher-led and offered free of charge, ensuring that every child has the opportunity to participate.
For specialised activities, we bring in external experts to provide high-quality instruction and inspiration.
Age-Appropriate Growth
— Our Extra-Curricular Programme is carefully tailored to be age-appropriate, ensuring that children at every stage of their Chandlings journey find activities that challenge and excite them:
Younger children might enjoy introductory sports, creative play, and nature exploration.
As they grow, children can take on more complex activities, join competitive teams, or dive deeper into specific areas of interest.
Older students have opportunities to develop leadership skills by mentoring younger children or taking on responsibilities within their chosen activities.
Nurturing Well-Rounded Individuals
Through our Extra-Curricular Programme, we aim to nurture well-rounded individuals who are curious, confident, and ready to embrace life’s challenges. As noted by Talk Education:
“Chandlings pupils have access to rather incredible opportunities – though every effort is made to not intimidate them or overwhelm them with choice.”
We believe in providing a wealth of opportunities while ensuring that each child feels supported in their choices. Our programme is designed to:
Foster new friendships across year groups
Develop teamwork and communication skills
Build resilience and problem-solving abilities
Encourage children to step out of their comfort zones and try new things
Create a sense of belonging and school pride
More Than Activities
Our Extra-Curricular Programme is more than just a list of activities, it’s an integral part of our commitment to nurturing childhood and preparing children for a bright future. We believe that these experiences outside the classroom are just as valuable as those within, helping to shape confident, curious, and capable young individuals.
Find Out More

pageCache.pageTitle: Performing Arts - Chandlings Independent Prep School - Oxford
pageCache.text:
Performing Arts
We believe that performing arts play a crucial role in a child’s development.
Fostering creativity, self-expression, and confidence. Our comprehensive arts programme is designed to inspire and nurture young talents from Nursery through to Year 6.
Specialist Teaching
— From Nursery onwards, all children benefit from specialist music and drama teaching.
Even our older Nursery children are introduced to the joys of music through weekly sessions with a professional singer.
This early exposure to the arts sets the stage for a lifelong appreciation and engagement with creativity.
Our Performing Arts department boasts a team of 15 visiting music teachers, many of whom are active professional musicians with Symphony Orchestras and local playhouses.
They provide over 150 Music and LAMDA lessons each week, offering our students the opportunity to learn from experienced practitioners. For those ready to showcase their skills, we prepare students for Associated Board, Trinity College, and LAMDA examinations.
Choirs & Public Speaking
— We believe that every child has a voice worth hearing.
From Year 1 to Year 6, all children participate in their Year Group Choir, performing at the Nine Lessons and Carols at Radley College and in our summer Arts Festival.
These experiences not only develop musical skills but also build confidence and teamwork.
For our younger performers, the Pre-Prep Choir offers an extra opportunity for those keen to explore their vocal talents. As children progress, they may be selected to join our Junior and Senior Chamber Choirs, with the Senior Choir even embarking on international tours.
Public speaking is nurtured through our annual whole-school Poetry Festival, culminating in a special performance where selected children from each year group showcase their skills to the school and parents.
Instrumental & Choral Speaking
Our extensive ensemble programme, featuring 16 different groups each week, allows children to explore various instruments and performance styles. Every ensemble performs at the Christmas Soiree and the Summer Arts Festival, providing regular opportunities for children to shine.
For those with a flair for the spoken word, our Senior Choral Speakers often compete and perform at prestigious events like the Edinburgh Fringe and Cheltenham Festivals. These experiences expose our students to diverse audiences and help them develop a deeper appreciation for the arts.
Performances
— We firmly believe that every child deserves their moment in the spotlight. Throughout the year, we offer numerous opportunities for children to perform.
Children delight audiences with their Nativity performances at the end of the first term.
Collaborate on a joint production in the spring term, fostering teamwork and creativity.
Children devise their own theatrical piece, which is then performed at the Summer Arts Festival.
Children finish their Chandlings journey with a final show at the end of the summer term.
What makes these productions truly special is that they are bespoke creations, written by our Heads of Music and Drama specifically for our students.
This tailored approach ensures that each child’s strengths are showcased and that the performances reflect the unique character of our school community.
At Chandlings Prep, we don’t just teach performing arts, we create an environment where every child can discover their artistic voice, build confidence, and develop a lifelong love for creative expression.
Find Out More

pageCache.pageTitle: Fees & Bursaries - Chandlings Independent Prep School - Oxford
pageCache.text:
Fees & Bursaries
Exceptional education should be accessible to families from diverse backgrounds.
We understand that choosing independent education is a significant investment in your child’s future, and we’re committed to providing transparency and support throughout this process.
Our fee structure is carefully reviewed each academic year to ensure we continue delivering the highest quality educational experience while maintaining value for our families. Current fee information is readily available through our detailed fee schedule, which outlines all aspects of your investment in your child’s education at Chandlings.
We also partner with YellowNest, an affordable childcare salary exchange scheme that may help eligible families reduce the cost of childcare by paying fees from their gross salary before tax and National Insurance deductions. Come & Visit Us
Experience the magic of childhood learning where every visit offers a glimpse into our vibrant educational community.
Throughout the year, we open our doors to welcome prospective families through two distinct experiences: our specialised Early Years Open Mornings in March and December, and our comprehensive Whole School Open Mornings in May and September.
During these interactive sessions, your children will become part of our learning adventure, participating in engaging activities that showcase our approach to education. As they explore, you’ll tour our exceptional facilities and most importantly, meet the heart of our school, our passionate pupils and dedicated staff who make Chandlings such a special place.
We understand that scheduled Open Mornings may not suit every family’s journey. That’s why we’re delighted to arrange personal tours during term time, offering you an intimate look at our school in action. These hour-long tours, beginning at either 9:30am or 1:30pm Monday to Friday, and conclude with refreshments with our Head.
We invite you to join us on:
Saturday 19 September 2026 (9:30 – 11:30am) Whole School Open Morning
Friday 9 October 2026 (9:30 – 11:30am) Wilderness Buggy Tours
Wednesday 9 December 2026 (9:30 – 11:30am) STEM Open Morning (Prep)
Our Registrar, Mrs Catriona Pitt (cpitt@chandlings.org.uk) is here to guide you through arranging your visit, whether you choose to attend an Open Morning or prefer a personal tour.

pageCache.pageTitle: Art, Design & Technology - Chandlings Independent Prep School - Oxford
pageCache.text:
Art, Design & Technology
We believe that creativity is a fundamental aspect of a child’s development.
Our Art, Design & Technology programme is designed to nurture imagination, develop practical skills, and encourage innovative thinking. We provide a rich and diverse curriculum that allows children to explore, experiment, and express themselves in unique ways.
Art
Our art department provides a nurturing environment where children’s creativity can flourish. Guided by specialist teachers, students embark on a journey of artistic discovery, developing their skills and confidence along the way.
From the earliest years, children are introduced to a wide range of artistic materials, tools, and techniques.
They learn to express their ideas visually, experimenting with different mediums and styles. As they progress, they develop a deeper understanding of drawing techniques, colour theory, and composition.
Our curriculum encourages children to explore art from different eras and cultures, fostering critical awareness and appreciation for diverse artistic expressions.
By studying both contemporary and historical artists, children learn to respond critically and creatively to different artistic styles, often linking their studies to their interests and topics in other subjects. We instil a sense of pride in every piece of work, showcasing achievements through displays and exhibitions, fostering confidence and a lifelong passion for the arts.
Design Technology
Design Technology at Chandlings is all about creative problem-solving.
Children learn to work independently and as part of a team, developing skills that are valuable far beyond the workshop.
They’re encouraged to evaluate their own work and the work of others critically, fostering an environment of constructive feedback and continuous improvement.
From hand tools to laser cutters and 3D printers, our young children have access to a range of equipment that brings their ideas to life in wood, metal, and plastic.
Our curriculum is designed to build skills progressively. Through a series of projects in Years 3, 4, and 5, children develop a strong foundation in design principles and practical skills. In Year 6, they apply these skills to pupil-led Young Enterprise projects, showcasing their creativity and entrepreneurial spirit.
We celebrate our students’ achievements by entering their brilliant work into national competitions and displaying examples around the school. For those keen to explore further, our co-curricular clubs offer extended learning opportunities in areas like Furniture Making and 3D Printing.
Food Technology
Our Food Technology programme is an exciting journey which starts in Year 3 as a specialist subject and continues through to Year 6. It’s a hands-on course that combines practical cooking skills with an understanding of nutrition and food origins.
We believe that cooking is an essential life skill, and our Food Technology classes are designed to equip children with knowledge about food, nutrition, and health.
They learn about food safety and are encouraged to make healthy choices. In our kitchen, children create a wide variety of dishes, including international cuisines, using different techniques to produce high-quality products.
From homemade breads and delicious salads to cakes and fresh pasta, our young chefs explore a world of flavours and textures.
Learning extends beyond the kitchen, with themed projects that bring history and culture to life. A highlight for our Year 3 students is preparing and hosting a Roman feast, complete with honey cake, flatbreads, and olives.
We encourage children to reflect on their culinary creations, discussing what they like and how recipes could be improved. This fosters critical thinking and creativity in the kitchen. Most importantly, we ensure that children enjoy the process of making food and are open to trying new flavours and dishes they may not have experienced before.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wrap-Around Care - Chandlings Independent Prep School - Oxford
pageCache.text:
Wrap-Around Care
We’ve designed our wrap-around care services to provide a seamless, supportive environment for your child, extending well beyond the regular school day. Our goal is to ensure that your child feels cared for, engaged, and happy at all times, while giving you the flexibility you need.
Breakfast Club
From 7:30am, we open our doors to early risers. Our Breakfast Club offers a warm, nurturing start to the day, complete with a nutritious breakfast to fuel young minds. Children can ease into their day in a relaxed atmosphere, enjoying social time with friends before starting their day. This service is available for an additional £10 per session.
Early Birds Club
For families who need a slightly earlier start but don’t require breakfast, our free Early Birds Club begins at 8am in the Lantern Hall. This supervised space allows children to arrive at school ahead of the main rush, giving them time to settle in and prepare for the day ahead.
After School Care
When the school bell rings, our care doesn’t stop.
We offer After School Care for Pre-Prep children and a Homework Club for Prep students, running from the end of the school day until 5pm, at no extra cost.
For our younger children in Pre-Prep, After School Care provides a natural extension to their day. In the Inner Hall, they engage in supervised play, continuing to learn through fun, age-appropriate activities.
Prep students benefit from our Homework Club, where they can complete assignments under the guidance of our staff. This structured time helps children develop good study habits and ensures they can relax at home, free from academic pressures.
Extended Hours
— We recognise that some families require care beyond 5pm, that’s why we offer an extended service until 6pm.
At 5pm, all children still at school are brought to the Inner Hall for collection. This service is available for an additional £10 per family per hour or part thereof.
We strive to make your family’s daily routine as smooth as possible, providing peace of mind that your child is in caring, capable hands. With Chandlings’ wrap-around care, you can balance your work commitments knowing that your child’s day is filled with enriching experiences and attentive care.
Find Out More

pageCache.pageTitle: Sports - Chandlings Independent Prep School - Oxford
pageCache.text:
Sports
Our approach to sports is rooted in the belief that physical activity should be enjoyable, inclusive, and character-building.
Championing Childhood Through Sport
At Chandlings, we understand that children learn best when they’re having fun. That’s why we prioritise making sports enjoyable for all our students. From our youngest learners to our oldest pupils, we focus on creating positive experiences that motivate children to engage fully in physical activities.
Traditional Games
Cricket, rugby, football, netball, and hockey form the backbone of our sports programme, teaching teamwork, strategy, and resilience.
Swimming
From Nursery to Year 6, all children benefit from our comprehensive swimming programme, developing water confidence and essential life skills.
Athletics
Our track and field activities help children discover their strengths in running, jumping, and throwing events.
Gymnastics
Through gymnastics, children develop flexibility, strength, and body awareness in a fun and challenging environment.
Competitive Opportunities
While we emphasise participation and personal growth, we also provide opportunities for those who thrive on competition. Regular fixtures against local prep schools allow our students to test their skills and learn valuable lessons about sportsmanship. For those showing exceptional talent, participation in IAPS tournaments offers the chance to compete on a broader scale, fostering ambition and a sense of achievement.
Learning Beyond the Game
Sports at Chandlings is about more than just physical skills. Through our sports programme, children learn important life lessons:
Teamwork and communication
Resilience and perseverance
Time management and discipline
Leadership and sportsmanship
The importance of a healthy, active lifestyle
To support our diverse sports programme, we are proud to offer excellent facilities:
Full-size Astroturf pitch
Multiple sports fields for various team games
Cross-country routes through our beautiful grounds
At Chandlings, we see sport as a powerful tool for championing childhood.
It’s a realm where children can play, explore, and challenge themselves in a supportive environment. Whether it’s the thrill of scoring their first goal, the satisfaction of mastering a new swimming stroke, or the joy of running freely across our fields, we believe these sporting experiences create lasting memories and contribute to a happy, healthy childhood.
Our approach to sports reflects our broader educational philosophy, we’re not just developing athletes; we’re nurturing well-rounded individuals. By balancing fun with skill development, inclusion with healthy competition, we aim to instil a love for physical activity that will stay with our children long after they leave Chandlings.

pageCache.pageTitle: Applying to Chandlings - Chandlings Independent Prep School - Oxford
pageCache.text:
Applying to Chandlings
Childhood doesn’t get much better than this
Our approach champions innovation, adventure and endeavour, always keeping the wellbeing of each individual child at the heart of everything we do. We create an environment where happy, healthy children naturally thrive in their learning journey.
Chandlings welcomes children from age 2 to 11 into a calm, joyful and nature‑rich school community where childhood is genuinely cherished. Our Nursery is the earliest entry point, reflecting our belief that the sooner a child’s love of learning is nurtured, the stronger the foundations for their future.
Children join us at many different stages of their educational journey, with Nursery, Reception and Year 3 being our most common entry points. We warmly welcome enquiries and applications for any year group throughout the school year, where places are available, and our friendly Admissions Team is here to guide and support you at every step.
The admissions journey at Chandlings is very much a partnership: time and care are taken on both sides to ensure the school is the right fit for each family, so that every child’s individual needs, interests and passions can be understood, supported, allowing them to flourish.
Entry Points
Please enter your childs date of birth to find out how to join us.
The next available year groups your child can join are:
Admissions: One Step At A Time
Joining Chandlings is a straightforward and supportive journey, designed to help families feel informed, welcomed and confident at every stage of the admissions process.
Step 1: Enquire Step 2: Visit Chandlings Step 3: Register your child Step 4: Arrange a taster day Step 5: Offer from Chandlings Step 6: Accept your new academic adventure
Our Admissions Team is here to guide you through each step, so please do get in touch if you have any questions along the way.
Visiting & Taster Days
Begin your journey by experiencing Chandlings firsthand through an Open Morning or personal tour. Following your visit, we’ll share our registration form, which can be returned along with a £100 registration fee to secure your place in our admissions process.
For our youngest learners joining Nursery or Reception, we arrange gentle taster sessions where they can meet their future friends and teachers in a relaxed setting. Children joining Years 1-6 spend a full day with us, experiencing our engaging curriculum while completing informal assessments in English and Mathematics.
Book an open morning
After Your Visit
Once your child’s visit has shown them to be ready for the Chandlings experience, we’ll extend a formal offer. A deposit of £750 secures their place, with Nursery deposits carrying forward to guarantee their Reception place.
You’ll then gain access to our comprehensive Admissions Portal and Welcome Pack, filled with everything you need to know about joining our community. Our \remains your personal guide throughout this journey, right up to welcoming you on your child’s first day.
